title: Great Stories of Faith — Reading and Writing Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of reading skills, writing, and figurative language!

questions.question: What are the five main elements of a narrative?
questions.explanation: The five main elements of a narrative are characters, setting, plot, conflict, and resolution. These work together to tell a complete story.

questions.question: What is a character trait?
options: A quality that describes what a person is like on the inside
questions.explanation: A character trait is a quality that describes what a person is like on the inside, such as brave, honest, kind, or faithful.

questions.question: Which figure of speech uses the words 'like' or 'as' to compare two things?
questions.explanation: A simile compares two things using the words 'like' or 'as.' For example, 'As the deer pants for streams of water, so my soul pants for you, my God' (Psalm 42:1).

questions.question: When Jesus said 'I am the bread of life,' what type of figurative language was He using?
questions.explanation: This is a metaphor because it compares two things without using 'like' or 'as.' Jesus compared Himself to bread to show that He is what our souls need to be satisfied.

questions.question: What is the first sentence of a well-organized paragraph called?
questions.explanation: The topic sentence is usually the first sentence of a paragraph. It tells the reader what the paragraph is about.

questions.question: Where would you find an index in a book?
options: At the front of the book
In the middle of the book
At the back of the book
On the cover of the book
questions.explanation: An index is found at the back of a book. It lists important words and topics in alphabetical order with page numbers.

questions.question: What is a Bible concordance used for?
options: Reading the Bible in a different language
Finding verses about a specific word or topic
questions.explanation: A Bible concordance helps you find verses about a specific topic or word. It is one of the most valuable tools for studying God's Word.

questions.question: When giving a book presentation, what should you NOT do?
options: Give away the ending of the story
Explain the lesson of the book
questions.explanation: You should avoid giving away the ending — called 'spoilers' — so your audience will be curious enough to read the book themselves.
